en.question: Why are XML tags recommended for separating sections of a complex Claude prompt?

options.text: Claude parses XML natively and handles other formats less reliably.
options.note: Claude handles plain text, markdown, and JSON perfectly well.

options.text: Tagged sections compress better, reducing the token cost of a long prompt.
options.note: Tags add tokens; the benefit is clarity rather than compression.

options.text: They mark unambiguous boundaries between instructions, examples, and data.
The API requires structured delimiters on any request that defines tools.
options.note: Tool use imposes no formatting requirement of this kind.

en.explanation: Clear delimiters let the model distinguish "this is your instruction" from "this is the document to operate on", which matters most when retrieved content might otherwise read as an instruction.
